밉다.m: hateful, detestable; annoying (often of a loved one)
밉다.x: I really can't stand the friend who lied.
밉다.e: In 미운 정 고운 정, Koreans say bonds grow through both annoyance and fondness.

존댓말.x: You use polite speech with people you've just met.
존댓말.t: Pronounced [존댄말] — the ㅅ between 존대 and 말 nasalizes to ㄴ.

재활용하다.ex: 다 마신 병은 깨끗이 씻어서 재활용하세요.
재활용하다.x: Rinse empty bottles clean and recycle them.

상권.x: The area around the subway station is a busy commercial district.
상권.e: Literally 'commerce circle' — the area where shops draw customers.

고혈압.ex: 아버지는 고혈압 때문에 매일 약을 드세요.
고혈압.x: My father takes medicine every day for high blood pressure.
고혈압.e: Literally 'high blood pressure' — a word-for-word match with English.

판단력.x: In urgent situations, quick judgment is needed.

입대.ex: 동생이 다음 달에 입대해서 가족들이 걱정하고 있어요.
입대.x: My younger brother enlists next month, so my family is worried.

슬기롭다.x: He solved the difficult problem wisely.
슬기롭다.e: 슬기 'wisdom' plus -롭다 'full of'; a native match for 지혜롭다.
슬기롭다.t: Seen in the drama title 슬기로운 의사생활, known in English as 'Hospital Playlist.'

끝으로.ex: 끝으로 오늘 와 주신 모든 분께 감사드립니다.
끝으로.x: In closing, I thank everyone who came today.
끝으로.t: Pronounced [끄트로]; typical for closing speeches and formal emails.

우여곡절.m: ups and downs, twists and turns
우여곡절.x: After many twists and turns, we ended up getting married.
우여곡절.e: Pictures a road that winds, bends and breaks before reaching the end.

신기록.x: That athlete set a new world record.

미역국을 먹다.m: to fail (an exam), to be rejected (lit. to eat seaweed soup)
미역국을 먹다.x: I prepared hard, but I flunked the interview.
미역국을 먹다.e: Seaweed is slippery, and 미끄러지다 'to slip' also means to fail an exam. A popular story also links it to 해산, meaning both 'disbanding' and 'giving birth' (after which mothers eat seaweed soup).
미역국을 먹다.t: Casual and humorous. This is why many Koreans avoid seaweed soup before exams and give sticky 엿 or 찹쌀떡 instead.

훈민정음.m: Hunminjeongeum, the original name of Hangeul
훈민정음.x: King Sejong created Hunminjeongeum for the common people.
훈민정음.e: Literally 'the correct sounds for teaching the people'.

촉매.ex: 그 사건은 사회 변화의 촉매 역할을 했습니다.
촉매.x: That incident served as a catalyst for social change.
촉매.e: Literally 'touching go-between' — it triggers a reaction without being used up.
촉매.t: Pronounced [총매]; used figuratively like English: 변화의 촉매가 되다.

전문성.x: This job requires a high level of expertise.

착수하다.m: to start, to embark on, to get down to (work)
착수하다.ex: 경찰은 그 사건에 대한 수사에 착수했습니다.
착수하다.x: The police launched an investigation into the case.
착수하다.e: Literally 'put your hands on' — getting your hands on a job.

합치하다.m: to agree, to coincide, to be in accord
합치하다.ex: 이번 협정에서 두 나라의 이해관계가 합치했습니다.
합치하다.x: In this agreement, the interests of the two countries coincided.

치닫다.forms: 치달아요 · 치달았어요 · 치달을 거예요 · 치달은 (+noun) (ㄷ irregular)
치닫다.m: to rush (toward), to escalate, to head toward (an extreme)
치닫다.ex: 두 나라의 갈등이 최악의 상황으로 치닫고 있습니다.
치닫다.x: The conflict between the two countries is heading toward the worst.
치닫다.e: 치- 'upward, intensely' + old verb 닫다 'to run': racing toward an extreme.
치닫다.t: Usually '~(으)로 치닫다' with 극단, 파국, 최악 — 'extreme, catastrophe, the worst'.

진퇴양난.m: a dilemma, being stuck between a rock and a hard place
진퇴양난.ex: 그는 진퇴양난에 빠져 어떻게 해야 할지 몰랐어요.
진퇴양난.x: He was stuck in a dilemma and didn't know what to do.
진퇴양난.e: Literally 'advancing and retreating are both hard'.

담을 쌓다.forms: 담을 쌓아요 · 담을 쌓았어요 · A와 담을 쌓고 지내다
담을 쌓다.m: to cut off ties with; to want nothing to do with
담을 쌓다.ex: 저는 학교 다닐 때 수학과 담을 쌓고 지냈어요.
담을 쌓다.x: Back in school, I wanted nothing to do with math.
담을 쌓다.e: Literally 'to build a wall' between yourself and something.

쐐기를 박다.m: to clinch; to settle something firmly; to nail it down
쐐기를 박다.x: The second-half goal clinched the win.
쐐기를 박다.e: 쐐기 = a wedge; driving it in locks things in place.

왕조.ex: 조선 왕조는 오백 년 넘게 이어졌습니다.
왕조.x: The Joseon Dynasty lasted for more than five hundred years.
왕조.e: Literally 'royal court', meaning a line of rulers.

입학사정관.x: The admissions officer carefully reviews the applicants' documents.
입학사정관.t: Pronounced [이팍싸정관] — ㅂ + ㅎ becomes ㅍ, and ㅅ after 학 becomes tense.

공예품.ex: 인사동에서 전통 공예품을 몇 개 샀어요.
공예품.x: I bought a few traditional handicrafts in Insa-dong.

명저.x: This book is regarded as a masterpiece of economics.

밥 먹듯 하다.forms: 거짓말을 밥 먹듯 해요 · 밥 먹듯이 (+verb)
밥 먹듯 하다.m: to do something all the time, as a habit (usually something bad) (lit. to do it like eating rice)
밥 먹듯 하다.ex: 그 친구는 약속을 어기는 걸 밥 먹듯 해요.
밥 먹듯 하다.x: That friend breaks promises all the time.
밥 먹듯 하다.e: Just as you eat rice every day without a second thought, the action has become routine.
밥 먹듯 하다.t: Mostly negative: 거짓말을 밥 먹듯 하다, 지각을 밥 먹듯 하다. Variant: 밥 먹듯이.

상소.ex: 판결에 불복하는 당사자는 상급 법원에 상소할 수 있습니다.
상소.x: A party who disputes a ruling can appeal to a higher court.
상소.e: Literally 'sue upward' — the umbrella term covering 항소 and 상고.

국민총소득.x: Per capita gross national income topped 30,000 dollars for the first time.
국민총소득.e: Literally 'total income of the nation's people'.

종합부동산세.ex: 비싼 집을 여러 채 가진 사람은 종합부동산세를 냅니다.
종합부동산세.x: People who own several expensive homes pay the comprehensive real estate tax.
종합부동산세.e: Literally 'comprehensive real-estate tax'; 부동산 is literally 'property that does not move.'
종합부동산세.t: Almost always shortened to 종부세 in the news.

종가.m: head family (main line of a clan), head house
종가.ex: 이 마을에는 오백 년 된 종가가 있어요.
종가.x: There is a five-hundred-year-old head family house in this village.
종가.e: Literally 'main-line house' — the eldest son's line of a clan.
종가.t: Often heard as 종갓집, especially when talking about traditional recipes passed down.
rel: eldest grandson of the main line

미시적.ex: 미시적 분석만으로는 전체 흐름을 알기 어렵습니다.
미시적.x: It's hard to grasp the overall trend with micro-level analysis alone.

필요악.x: Many people think of competition as a necessary evil.
필요악.e: Literally 'needed evil', matching the English phrase.
필요악.t: Pronounced [피료악]: the ㄹ links to the next syllable.
